Subject: Competitive eval: model quality follow-up (Acme AI)

Samir/Jenna —

Thanks again for the call today — great to learn more about the customer support use case and the set of failure modes you care most about (hallucinations on policy & legal content, tone preservation, and short-answer accuracy on knowledge cutoff items). Per our discussion, I pulled together the high-level recap and next steps so we have alignment on what to test next: 

Summary of ask
- Evaluate hallucination rates and factuality on a 250-prompt subset (mix of policy, product, and knowledge cutoff items)
- Run regression checks vs the hyperscaler baseline you quoted (HyperscalerX endpoints) and the current Redwood hosted model (rwd-4.1)
- Surface token/time cost delta and a few latency p50/p95 points for typical 128-token responses

Immediate next steps (owners)
- Samir: confirm the 250-prompt set is representative (you mentioned ~40% policy/legal, 40% product KB lookups, 20% short-answer). If that looks right we’ll proceed.
- Aditya: we’ll run the Redwood vs HyperscalerX A/B on the 250 prompts and produce a CSV of per-prompt outputs + hallucination flags.
- Rishi: coord on any redlines/PII handling requirements and provide the minimal privacy constraints we should encode for inference.

Deliverables by EOD Wednesday (Nov 4)
- Per-prompt comparison CSV (attached as acme_eval_results_v1.csv)
- Prompt set used (acme_prompt_set_v2.json)
- Short slide: Redwood vs HyperscalerX model-quality summary (redwood-vs-hyperscaler-comparison.pdf)

Notes on evaluation methodology we proposed on the call
- Blind eval: outputs will be shuffled so annotators don’t see the source engine.
- Hallucination heuristics: annotators will mark any unsupported factual claim or invented citation. We’ll also run an automated n-gram overlap and citation check for quick triage.
- Regression checks: diff run against your previous baselines (please confirm the HyperscalerX model id/version you want us to compare).

Attachments: acme_prompt_set_v2.json (prompt canonicalization + expected labels), redwood-vs-hyperscaler-comparison.pdf (executive summary)

Thanks — I’ll wait for the confirmation on prompt mix and hyperscaler model id and start the runs once we have those.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.infra
+1 (415) 555-0198

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. That all looks great — confirm the prompt mix you listed is correct. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Hyperscaler baseline
- We want HyperscalerX v2.7.3 (the same endpoint our current prod is hitting). Please label it HyperscalerX-v2.7.3 in the CSV so our ops folks can map rows back to their internal tests.

2) Annotator guidance
- For hallucination flags, can you include a short freeform field where annotators can paste the part of the output they judged as hallucinated? That helps us debug.

3) Privacy constraints
- We can share a redacted knowledge base for the product KB prompts but need to ensure no customer PII leaves our environment. If you need local evaling, can Redwood run the evaluation in a private VPC project? If not, we can provide a sanitized sample.

If you can confirm the Hyperscaler model label and whether a private VPC evaluation is possible, we’ll be good to go.

—Samir

We’ve kicked off the runs this morning. Quick update and plan: 

What we’re running
- Redwood rwd-4.1 (hosted) vs HyperscalerX v2.7.3 (their prod endpoint)
- 250 prompts (per the shared prompt_set_v2). 3 seeds for stochastic sampling where applicable to capture variance.

Evaluation instrumentation
- Per-prompt outputs will be saved to acme_eval_results_v1.csv with the following columns: prompt_id, prompt_text, model, output_text, hallucination_flag, hallucination_excerpt, factuality_score, latency_ms, token_cost_usd, run_seed

- We can run the same tests in a private VPC for Acme but it requires a short legal/ops handshake and a scoped SOW (approx 2-3 business days to stand up infra and sign-off). For the EOD Wed deliverable we’ll run a sanitized sample in hosted and flag any prompts that must be re-run in-VPC.

ETA
- Sanitized-run CSV + slides: EOD Wed (Nov 4) — attached CSV will include preliminary hallucination flags from our automated checks; manual annotation to follow (we’ll include annotator fields once complete).
- VPC-run timeline: estimate 3 business days after SOW approval.

Attachments: acme_eval_results_v1.csv (partial/stub), redwood-vs-hyperscaler-comparison.pdf (draft)

Let me know if you want us to include additional instrumented metrics (e.g., token-level logits or top-k divergence) — we can add that as a follow-on if needed.
